onset.Description: Seconds from the first sample of the macro-iEEG recording. Computed as source_start_time + 10 s - first LFP timestamp: the source behavioural/TTL clock has movie onset (TTL 4) at 0 s, while the stored LFP starts 10 s before movie onset (LFP_PAD) and its timestamps are relative to that padded start.

duration.Description: stop_time - start_time for trials; 0 for TTL markers and movie frames.

sample.Description: round(onset * SamplingFrequency), zero-based sample index into the recording.

Levels.encoding: Movie watching phase (one interval per run); source trials table row with stim_phase=encoding.
Levels.recognition: One new/old recognition trial (frame shown until response); source trials table.
Levels.ttl: TTL marker from acquisition/events_ttl; code in value.
Levels.experiment_id: Task-id marker from acquisition/experiment_ids (only when not aligned with TTLs).
Levels.movie_frame: Movie frame presentation time from stimulus/presentation/movieframe_time.

value.Description: TTL code. Source description: The events correspond to the TTL markers for each session. The TTL markers are the following: 4 = start of the movie, 40-49 = frame number mapping to a log file, 33 = keypress, 7 = start probe for recognition, 9 = startITI, 1 = start fixation, 10 = end fixation, 52 = screen of instruction, 66 = end of experiment Codes 0 and 32 also occur in a few source files but are not described by the source.

Levels.40: frame number mapping to a log file (40-49)
Levels.41: frame number mapping to a log file (40-49)
Levels.42: frame number mapping to a log file (40-49)
Levels.43: frame number mapping to a log file (40-49)
Levels.44: frame number mapping to a log file (40-49)
Levels.45: frame number mapping to a log file (40-49)
Levels.46: frame number mapping to a log file (40-49)
Levels.47: frame number mapping to a log file (40-49)
Levels.48: frame number mapping to a log file (40-49)
Levels.49: frame number mapping to a log file (40-49)

experiment_id.Description: Experiment/task id recorded at the same timestamp as the TTL. Source description: The experimentid (or task_id) corresponds to the encoding (i.e., movie watching as one trial) or recognition trials. The encoding is indexed by: 2. The recognition trials are indexed by: 3.

movie_frame.Description: Movie frame label as stored in the source. Source description: Movie frame numbers associated with time instances during the encoding (movie watching) phase [starts counting from 0--Python way]

stimulus_file.Description: Source stimulus file name (stimulus images/movie are copyrighted and are not distributed). The file name for the stimulus

actual_response.Description: The button pressed during experiment, 1-6, where 1:new-sure, 2:new-unsure, 3:new-guessing, 4:old-guessing, 5:old-unsure, 6:old-sure

response_confidence.Description: The confidence level of response (1=guessing, 2=unsure, 3=sure) for each each new/old trial

response_correct.Description: Whether the response was correct=1 or incorrect=0 for each new/old trial

response_time.Description: Response latency for recognition trials = source_response_time - source_start_time. n/a for encoding (no response).

source_start_time.Description: Original start time in the source session clock (movie onset = 0).

source_stop_time.Description: Original trial stop time in the source session clock.

source_response_time.Description: Original NWB trials.response_time (absolute time in the source session clock, not a latency). The response time for each new/old trial

source_trial_id.Description: Row id of the source NWB trials table.
